title: Rhodesia Declares Itself a Republic
reason: The event is real but dated to the wrong year. On 20 June 1969 Rhodesia held a referendum in which the predominantly white electorate approved (a) becoming a republic and (b) a new constitution entrenching white minority rule — that referendum did happen in 1969. However, the actual declaration/proclamation of the republic (severing formal ties to the British Crown, replacing the Governor with a ceremonial President) did not occur until 2 March 1970, after Parliament passed the new constitution in November 1969. Multiple independent sources (Wikipedia's dedicated 1969 referendum article, the general Rhodesia article, and Britannica) are explicit that Rhodesia 'declared itself a republic' on 2 March 1970 — a full 8+ months after the 1969 vote. Since the title/description describe the declaration itself ('held a...referendum and declared Rhodesia a republic'), and the join-key year here is 1969, the year is wrong per the hard rules (event materially happened, but in 1970, not 1969). Note also a secondary, non-decisive nuance: the referendum was not strictly 'whites-only' — a small number of Africans (~6,600) voted on a separate, discriminatory 'B' roll alongside ~81,500 white 'A' roll voters — but this doesn't change the year verdict. The 'recognized by no foreign government' claim checks out for both dates (only South Africa and Portugal maintained informal diplomatic/consular ties; no state extended formal recognition).
